name: Post-Punk
def: Punk's energy redirected into art-school experimentation — angular basslines, cavernous production, dub space and emotional ambiguity.

traits.v: Cold, cavernous, reverb-and-dub-treated space.
Angular, melodic, lead basslines.
Minor-key, dissonant, art-damaged.

why: It keeps punk's tension but opens it into cold, spacious production and angular, bass-led arrangements.

tracks.why: Hannett's icy, spacious production invented the cold atmosphere dream pop later warmed.

name: Gothic Rock
def: Post-punk's gloom made theatre — tribal drums, chorused bass, cavernous reverb and baritone drama in black lace.

traits.v: Chorused, flanged guitar in cathedral reverb.
Tribal toms and driving, melodic bass.
Low, theatrical baritone croon.
The Batcave and black-clad club culture.

why: It aestheticises post-punk's darkness — romantic, macabre and ritualistic rather than austere.

tracks.why: Nine minutes of dub-spaced dread that founded goth in one take.

name: Industrial
def: Anti-music from the factory floor — tape loops, machine noise, synth rot and transgressive performance, weaponising the sounds of industry.

traits.v: Metal percussion, tape hiss, corroded synths.
Loops, cut-ups and studio-as-weapon process.
Mail-art networks, provocation and post-industrial decay.

why: It treats noise, machinery and tape manipulation as the music itself — the studio turned against comfort.

tracks.why: Queasy tape-and-synth dread — anti-music as pure atmosphere.

name: Dream Pop
def: Gauzy, reverb-soaked pop prioritising texture and mood over riffs — breathy vocals floating in shimmering, effects-laden guitar.

traits.v: Reverb-drenched, chorused, shimmering guitar.
Breathy, melodic, mixed into the haze.
Atmosphere foregrounded over attack.

why: It warms post-punk's cold space into lush reverb, with vocals and guitar blurred into mood.

tracks.why: A wordless vocal used as pure texture showed melody could dissolve into atmosphere.

name: Noise Pop
def: Sweet pop melodies buried under squalls of feedback and distortion — sugar and noise in equal, deliberate measure.

traits.v: Pop hooks drowned in feedback and fuzz.
Bright girl-group and bubblegum melody.
Distortion treated as a pop sweetener.

why: It fuses bubblegum melody with walls of feedback so that noise and pop become a single gesture.

name: Ethereal Wave
def: The gothic-adjacent, cathedral-reverb wing of dream pop — wordless, operatic vocals over shimmering, melancholic guitar and synth.

traits.v: Soaring, often wordless soprano used as texture.
Vast reverb, chorus-drenched guitar, cold synth pads.
Romantic, melancholic, modal.

why: Massed reverb and a vocal used purely as floating texture create a weightless, cathedral-like space.

name: Shoegaze
def: Walls of layered, effects-saturated guitar where melody, vocal and noise blur into one overwhelming texture — named for the pedalboard stare. Also called 'dream rock', it grew up inside the UK indie scene as its dreamiest wing.

traits.v: Pitch-bending glide guitar and dense layered fuzz.
Androgynous vocals buried inside the wall of sound.
Maximal layering; the mix as the instrument.
Major-key drift smeared by detune and tremolo.

why: Washed-out guitar layering and glide-based lead phrasing dissolve melody, vocal and noise into a single overwhelming texture.

tracks.why: Shields' pitch-bending glide guitar is the defining timbre the genre is measured against.

name: Neo-Psychedelia
def: A modern reworking of 60s psychedelia's drones, fuzz and studio haze through post-punk and indie sensibilities.

traits.v: Fuzz, phasing and reverb recombined with indie jangle.
Modal, drone-leaning vamps.
Hazy, layered, lo-fi-to-lush.

why: It reapplies 60s psychedelic studio textures — drones, fuzz, phasing — within a post-punk and indie framework.

tracks.t: Feels Like We Only Go Backwards

name: Nu-Gaze
def: The second shoegaze wave — mid-2000s bands reviving the wall of sound with alt-rock scale and electronic gloss, a decade after the first wave burned out. Also called 'second-wave shoegaze'.

traits.v: Classic glide-guitar wash rebuilt with modern high-gain and synth layers.
Bigger and cleaner than the first wave — alt-radio scale.
Blog-era indie; the bridge generation that kept the sound alive.

why: It revives shoegaze's glide-guitar textures at alt-rock scale, carrying the sound across the 2000s and 2010s.

tracks.why: The second wave’s breakout — Loveless textures rebuilt for 2000s alt radio.

name: Slowcore
def: Indie rock slowed to a crawl and stripped bare — hushed vocals, clean guitar and glacial tempos that leave silence as part of the arrangement. The quiet refusal of grunge's loudness.

traits.v: Glacial tempos; every beat left exposed.
Hushed, close-mic, often harmonised.
Clean, sparse guitar with room and reverb doing the arranging.
90s American indie playing quiet rooms while grunge filled arenas.

why: It inverts the era's volume — dream pop's haze slowed and hollowed out until restraint itself becomes the intensity.

tracks.why: Two voices over near-silence — slowcore's restraint as its own intensity.

name: Coldwave
def: The French cousin of post-punk — cheap synths, drum machines and detached, minor-key vocals delivering an icy, minimal chill.

traits.v: Thin, icy synths and clattering drum machines.
Detached, deadpan, often French-language delivery.
Stark minor-key minimalism.
French DIY cassette and small-label culture.

why: It freezes post-punk further — machine rhythm and affectless vocals stripped of all warmth or gloss.

name: New Post-Punk
def: The post-punk revival that began in Bristol, South London and Dublin around 2017 — IDLES, Shame and Fontaines D.C. pairing punk abrasion, spoken-sung vocals and literate, political lyrics with a return to post-punk's bass-led tension.

traits.v: Shouted or spoken-sung, accent-forward, wry and political.
Driving, bass-led post-punk drive with hardcore-punk attack.
Bristol, the Brixton Windmill and Dublin, 2017 on — a DIY guitar-band resurgence scaled to festival headliner.

why: It revives post-punk's angular, bass-led tension and deadpan vocal for a new generation of literary guitar bands.

tracks.why: Bristol 2017 — a one-chord bass pulse, bellowed class politics and hardcore attack announcing the wave.

name: Art Pop
def: Pop songcraft as a canvas for high-concept art — auteur voices, surreal imagery and production experiment inside the three-minute song.

traits.v: Auteur-controlled, experiment-forward studio craft.
Idiosyncratic, theatrical, instantly identifiable voices.
Pop forms warped by concept — songs as short films.

why: It keeps pop’s hooks but hands the whole frame to a single auteur vision, so the production concept is the song.

tracks.t: Running Up That Hill (A Deal with God)
tracks.why: A Fairlight-built art song that is also an undeniable pop single — the genre’s balance in one track.

tempoNote: Song-by-song — the production concept outranks tempo.

name: Sprechgesang
def: Deadpan spoken-sung delivery over wiry post-punk — Schoenberg’s speech-song reborn as the defining voice of 2020s art rock.

traits.v: Dry, conversational speech pitched against the band.
Angular, bass-led post-punk drive.
Observational, ironic, hyper-specific detail.
The Brixton Windmill circuit and its diaspora.

why: Removing melody from the voice puts all expression into rhythm and text — speech becomes the lead instrument.

tracks.why: Florence Shaw’s flat, found-text monotone over taut post-punk defined the wave.

name: Zoomergaze
def: The fourth shoegaze wave — Gen-Z bedroom producers building the wall of sound in a DAW, breaking songs on TikTok and SoundCloud before ever playing a show.

traits.v: DAW-native — plugin fuzz walls and programmed drums from a laptop.
Digital glide-guitar smear, often heavier and more compressed than the first wave.
TikTok, SoundCloud and Discord scenes; the song travels before the band exists.

why: It rebuilds shoegaze's overwhelming texture with bedroom-pop tools and internet-native distribution — the wall of sound as a solo laptop project.

tracks.why: A TikTok-born wall of sound — the fourth wave announcing itself.

name: Dark Post-Punk
def: The coldwave and goth strain of post-punk revived for a global generation — icy drum machines, chorused bass and grey-concrete melancholy.

traits.v: Chorused bass, icy synths, drum-machine pulse.
Low, detached, often non-English baritone.
Post-Soviet and Latin American scenes gone global via streaming.

why: It re-runs 1980–83 coldwave through modern doomer aesthetics — the same cold palette, recharged by new geographies.

tracks.why: A Belarusian coldwave song going TikTok-viral announced the revival’s reach.

name: Darkwave
def: Goth’s atmosphere carried onto synthesizers — minor-key electronic melancholy between gothic rock, synth pop and ethereal wave.

traits.v: Synth pads and drum machines under gothic guitar and bass.
Minor keys and suspended, unresolved pads.
Solemn, reverb-draped, often duetted.

why: It proves the goth sensibility survives the loss of the rock band — mood carried entirely by electronics.

tracks.why: 4AD gloom on sequencers — the bridge from goth rock into electronic darkness.

name: Witch House
def: Occult-themed internet electronics — ethereal, pitched-down vocals and blown-out drum-machine beats buried in heavy reverb, noise and darkwave gloom.

traits.v: Dense reverb, tape hiss and corroded, noisy synths.
Ethereal, screwed or reversed, often unintelligible.
Slow, screwed hip-hop and trap drum-machine patterns.
Blog- and SoundCloud-native; triangle-and-cross typography.

why: It runs goth atmosphere through Houston's screwed tempo — darkwave's mood rebuilt from slowed rap production instead of a band.

tracks.why: A screwed choral sample over trap drums — the whole genre in one track.

tempoNote: Often a 120–140 trap pulse heard at half time.

name: 2000s Post-Punk Revival
def: New York and British guitar bands reviving 1978–82 — Joy Division basslines, Television and Gang of Four guitar, tight trousers and a dancefloor pulse — from Is This It and Turn On the Bright Lights to Franz Ferdinand and Bloc Party.

traits.v: Driving, disco-tinged hi-hat eighths under melodic lead bass.
Clean, trebly, interlocking guitars; reverb and chorus in the Interpol/Editors wing.
Detached baritone croon or clipped, nervy yelp.
Lower East Side New York 2001–03, then Glasgow, London and Leeds; NME-fuelled and festival-scaled by 2005.

why: It rebuilt post-punk's angular guitar and bass interplay with the tighter, brighter production of the 2000s, trading the original's dread for dancefloor energy.

tracks.why: Lead bass, chiming guitars and a flat baritone — the Joy Division template rerun with 2002 clarity.

tempoNote: Dancefloor-fast; 'Take Me Out' famously halves its tempo for the main riff.

name: Windmill Art-Punk
def: The South London scene centred on the Windmill pub in Brixton and producer Dan Carey — black midi, Squid, Black Country, New Road and Dry Cleaning — fusing post-punk with math rock, no wave, krautrock and chamber instrumentation into through-composed, often improvised art-rock.

traits.v: Through-composed, multi-section pieces that build from improvisation rather than verse–chorus.
Odd meters, abrupt tempo shifts and motorik lock-grooves, often with a virtuoso drummer leading.
Clean, angular guitars against saxophone, violin and synth; dynamics from whisper to full noise.
The Windmill, Brixton, and Speedy Wunderground, 2017–22 — a small venue scene signed en masse to Rough Trade, Warp, 4AD and Ninja Tune.

why: A single tiny venue let bands develop by playing to each other, so technical ambition and formal experiment were rewarded over hooks, and post-punk's tension was re-routed through math rock and no wave.

tracks.why: A single bass note, Morgan Simpson's drumming and Geordie Greep's strangled sprechgesang — the Windmill sound at its most reduced and most extreme.
